stories.title: Business schools defend their relevance
stories.summary: An IIM Bangalore professor argues that MBA programs remain vital for developing responsible leaders despite recent calls for their abolition. Critics, including a Cambridge professor, suggest traditional business schools provide a limited understanding of real-world mechanics. The debate over the value of the degree continues.

stories.title: AI shifts entry-level hiring patterns
stories.summary: A report from the Burning Glass Institute and RAISE US finds that AI is reducing hiring for entry-level white-collar roles. While widespread job losses have not occurred, white-collar industries now employ 1.5 million fewer workers than pre-pandemic trends suggested. Gateway careers are becoming harder to find.

stories.title: AI to handle routine tasks in organisations
stories.summary: Dr Pramod Kumar, founder of ISB&M, predicts that AI will manage 50 to 60 percent of routine tasks in the coming years. He suggests that human judgment and strategic thinking will become more essential as machines and humans increasingly work together in the modern workplace.

stories.title: Santa Ynez High students get firsthand look at local careers in the trades - Santa Maria Times
Rutgers launches Alzheimer’s research program for students
stories.summary: Rutgers University has launched a five-year program to train medical students in Alzheimer’s research. Funded by the National Institute on Aging with a $353,295 grant, the initiative will pair up to 10 students each summer with faculty mentors who hold active NIH research portfolios.

stories.title: Vanderbilt students complete New York City co-op
stories.summary: Headstart Careers and iXperience placed 11 Vanderbilt University students in New York City roles during the Fall 2026 semester. The inaugural cohort worked in fields including finance, AI and law. More than 10 employer offers have already been extended to the students for Spring 2027.

stories.title: Allcargo Group to open logistics school in Pune
stories.summary: The Allcargo Group is partnering with FUEL SkillTech and Entrepreneurship University to establish the Allcargo School of Logistics. The group has committed Rs 15 crore to the project, which aims to provide logistics training and fully funded MBA scholarships to 100 students from underprivileged backgrounds.

stories.title: BHEL opens recruitment for trainee positions
stories.summary: BHEL is accepting applications for 415 Supervisor Trainee and Executive Trainee posts. The state-owned engineering firm is seeking candidates to fill these roles as part of its ongoing workforce expansion. Details regarding eligibility and the application process are available through the company's official recruitment portal.

stories.title: NPS Yeshwanthpur wins Children’s Earthshot award
stories.summary: National Public School, Yeshwanthpur, secured first prize in the Clean Our Air category at the 2026 Children’s Earthshot Awards. The school was the only representative from Karnataka among 15 national finalists. The team will receive a $2,000 grant to further develop their air filtration innovation.

stories.title: Teacher named district champion at ASTRA Awards
stories.summary: Theeba Yellapan of SJKT Somasundram has been named District Champion in the Best Educational Technology Teacher category at the ASTRA Awards 2026. The recognition highlights her work in integrating technology and innovative practices into the classroom to improve student engagement.

stories.title: Alphores student qualifies for national dodgeball championship
stories.summary: T. Gautham, a Class X student at Alphores E-Techno School, has been selected to compete in the National-Level Sub-Junior Dodgeball Championship. He earned his spot after a state-level performance in Jagityal. The national event is scheduled for December 26 and 27 in Jammu and Kashmir.

stories.title: Joburg school recognized for global awards
stories.summary: A Johannesburg principal and an online school have been shortlisted for international education awards. The recognition highlights new approaches to traditional schooling, including the removal of homework and the implementation of digital management systems. The winners will be announced in the coming months.

stories.title: Dhruv Global School student wins basketball medals
stories.summary: Jui Godbole, a Class VIII student, won gold at the 51st Sub-Junior State-Level Basketball Championship and silver at the national level. Following her performance in Vijayawada, she has been selected for state-level trials for the School Games competition.

stories.title: VRS student selected for national volleyball
stories.summary: Bhaktu Akhira, a student at Vivekananda Residential School in Karimnagar, has been selected for national-level volleyball competitions. The event is scheduled to take place in Shirdi, Maharashtra, from November 24 to 28. The student qualified following his performance at the state level.

stories.title: Prime Minister applauds student painting
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi praised a painting by Ishita, a Class 9 student at Kendriya Vidyalaya, Ambala Cantt. The artwork depicts the daily routine of students during examination periods. The Prime Minister is scheduled to interact with students regarding exam stress on November 27.

stories.title: Grade 8 student wins world robotics championship
stories.summary: Reiniza Kate Ulgasan, 14, won the championship trophy and a gold medal in Sumo Robot Junior Basic at the World Robot Games in Japan. The student from Julio Ledesma National High School also secured multiple silver and bronze medals across various robotics categories.

stories.title: Beacon School learners compete in robotics olympiad
stories.summary: Beacon School, a facility for learners with special needs, participated in the national World Robot Olympiad for the second consecutive year. Students used LEGO kits to build and program robots to navigate obstacle courses. The school remains the only special needs institution from the Western Cape participating.

stories.title: Indian student projects featured at Riyadh innovation fair
stories.summary: Indian students and innovators are presenting projects at the Security and Innovation Fair in Riyadh. Entries include clean energy solutions and drone technology designed to minimize environmental disturbance. The event runs from November 24 to 26 at the Riyadh International Convention and Exhibition Center.

stories.title: UGC-run BdREN team wins UN global AI hackathon - Daily Sun
NIT Jamshedpur researcher wins Young Scientist Award
stories.summary: Rajkumar Mandal, a research scholar at NIT Jamshedpur, received the Young Scientist Award at the 7th URSI Regional Conference on Radio Science. Mandal was recognised for his paper on satellite-based positioning accuracy in agricultural fields. The research examines GNSS positioning in both open and canopy agricultural environments.

stories.title: IIT Bombay and HKUST form sustainability partnership
stories.summary: IIT Bombay and the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology have signed a memorandum of understanding to collaborate on green energy and sustainability research. The partnership aims to promote knowledge exchange and experiential learning, using university campuses as platforms for sustainability experimentation and solutions.

stories.title: IIT Bombay and HKUST partner on living lab initiative
stories.summary: IIT Bombay and the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology have partnered to advance campus sustainability through a Living Lab approach. The agreement was signed during HKUST Living Lab Week to facilitate the testing of sustainability solutions within campus environments by faculty and students.

stories.title: BITS Pilani launches M.Tech in Robotics and Autonomous Systems
stories.summary: BITS Pilani WILP has introduced a new M.Tech program focused on Robotics and Autonomous Systems. The program is designed for working professionals, adding to the institution's existing portfolio of education and career-focused offerings for students and job seekers.

stories.title: Swindon students visit Nationwide for career day
stories.summary: Pupils from Swindon Academy participated in a workplace experience day at Nationwide's head office. The session was part of KPMG’s Opening Doors to Opportunities programme, which aims to improve career readiness and confidence among young people by providing exposure to professional environments.

stories.title: ESA opens applications for Earth Observation award
stories.summary: The European Space Agency is accepting applications for the 2027 Earth Observation Excellence Award. The prize, which offers up to 15,000 euros, recognises early-career researchers who use satellite data to address climate change, environmental challenges, and societal needs.

stories.title: Medical University of Turkmenistan hosts biology olympiad
stories.summary: The V International Internet Olympiad in Biology was held at the Myrat Garryyev State Medical University of Turkmenistan. The event attracted over 300 students from 16 countries who completed tests and problems in various biological fields over a 150-minute digital competition.

stories.title: CBSE releases biology practice questions for 2027 exams
stories.summary: The CBSE has provided a set of 100 multiple-choice questions for Class 12 biology students ahead of the 2027 board exams. The resource aims to help students familiarise themselves with the latest syllabus, marking schemes, and objective question patterns.

stories.title: CBSE provides history practice questions for 2027 exams
stories.summary: Students preparing for the 2027 CBSE Class 12 history board exams have been provided with 100 multiple-choice questions. The practice set covers all twelve chapters across three themes, intended to help students improve chronological memory and understand the current examination pattern.

stories.title: CISCE outlines ISC Class 11 history exam structure
stories.summary: The CISCE has released the exam pattern for the 2027 ISC Class 11 history assessment. The 100-mark evaluation includes an 80-mark written theory paper. Students are encouraged to familiarise themselves with the structure early to manage study time between Indian and World History.

stories.title: CISCE details ISC Class 11 geography exam structure
stories.summary: The CISCE has published the 2027 exam pattern for ISC Class 11 geography. The 100-mark assessment includes a 70-mark written theory paper. The board suggests early review of the structure to assist students in organising their study of physical geography and practical fieldwork.

stories.title: RBSE releases Class 11 maths syllabus for 2026-27
stories.summary: The Rajasthan Board of Secondary Education has prescribed the Class 11 mathematics syllabus for the 2026-27 academic session. The curriculum covers 14 chapters, including calculus and statistics. The final examination will be worth 100 marks with a duration of three hours and 15 minutes.

stories.title: CBSE plans assessment shift for classes 10 and 12
stories.summary: The CBSE is planning to revise its assessment system for classes 10 and 12 to prioritise conceptual understanding over rote learning. The proposed framework, aligned with the National Education Policy 2020, aims to reduce student reliance on memorised answers during board examinations.

stories.title: Report details hidden costs of teacher training
stories.summary: A Discovery Education blog post highlights that teacher training costs extend beyond registration fees. Districts are advised to account for staff time, substitute coverage, and coaching salaries. The report suggests that professional development is most effective when focused on specific, measurable priorities.

stories.title: Ellis Elementary students lead parent conferences
stories.summary: Students at Ellis Elementary School recently hosted their own parent-teacher conferences. Instead of traditional teacher-led meetings, students presented their own progress, goals, and reflections on challenges they have overcome to their families.

stories.title: Bermuda Mathematics Academy sees record olympiad turnout
stories.summary: The Bermuda Mathematics Academy hosted 21 participants at its Fall Maths Olympiad, marking a record increase from the two students who attended the inaugural event. The competition was split between middle and high school problem sets, with one-third of participants being female.

stories.title: Turkmenistan announces biology olympiad winners
stories.summary: The V International Online Biology Olympiad in Turkmenistan has concluded, with 164 students receiving awards. The winners included 88 representatives from the host country and 76 international participants.

stories.title: III International Internet Olympiad in Finance held in Turkmenistan
stories.summary: Students from 72 universities in Turkmenistan and ten foreign countries solved 10 financial tasks in 120 minutes. A total of 121 prize places were awarded, with Turkmen students achieving the best results. The competition tested financial knowledge across international borders.

stories.title: RMO 2026 provisional scores expected by December 5
stories.summary: Provisional scores for the Regional Mathematical Olympiad are expected by December 5, 2026. Students can access marks through the official Homi Bhabha Centre for Science Education portal. These preliminary results remain subject to verification and final cutoff adjustments before the official INMO 2027 selection list is declared.

stories.title: Delhi High Court declines to intervene in DU master's seat dispute
stories.summary: The Delhi High Court refused to direct Delhi University to create additional master's seats for its first four-year undergraduate batch. The court asked the University Grants Commission to decide on student complaints within three weeks, noting that administrative decisions fall outside the court's remit.

stories.title: India A batter Vaibhav Sooryavanshi draws praise after double century
stories.summary: Following a 53-ball 204 in the Rising Stars Asia Cup, 15-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has received calls from former players to join the senior team. Mohammed Kaif questioned why the teenager is not currently playing in T20I cricket after his performance against the United Arab Emirates.

stories.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi hits 52-ball double century
stories.summary: Fifteen-year-old Vaibhav Sooryavanshi scored 204 runs off 53 balls during a Rising Stars Asia Cup match in Doha. The innings included a 28-ball century and 28 sixes, setting a series of world records. India A defeated the United Arab Emirates by seven wickets.

stories.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi powers India A to semi-finals
stories.summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi scored an unbeaten 204 off 53 balls to secure India A's place in the ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 semi-finals. The 15-year-old's performance followed two lower-scoring outings against Nepal and Pakistan A. His knock included a record-breaking display of power-hitting.

stories.title: Durham University offers scholarships for Pakistani students
stories.summary: Durham University is offering the Inspiring Excellence Undergraduate Scholarship 2027 for international students starting in September 2027. Awards range from £15,000 to £30,000 over three years. The scholarship is competitive and does not cover accommodation, living expenses, or travel costs.

stories.title: University of St Andrews offers fully funded scholarship
stories.summary: The University of St Andrews is offering one International Excellence Scholarship 2027 to an outstanding international student. The award covers 100 percent of tuition fees for the duration of an undergraduate degree. The scholarship is highly competitive and open to applicants from several countries.

stories.title: University of Wollongong in Dubai offers merit scholarships
stories.summary: The University of Wollongong in Dubai is offering tuition fee discounts of 15, 25, or 50 percent for students enrolling in the Winter 2027 trimester. The merit-based scholarships are available to high-achieving international applicants but do not cover living expenses or other study-related costs.

stories.title: University of Kent offers master's scholarship for Pakistani students
stories.summary: The University of Kent is offering a £5,000 tuition fee stipend for international students from selected countries, including Pakistan, starting a postgraduate master's degree in January 2027. The award is a partial scholarship and does not cover living, accommodation, or travel costs.

stories.title: Chinese Government Scholarship 2027/2028 applications open
stories.summary: The Chinese Government Scholarship is accepting applications for the 2027/2028 academic year. The program offers financial support for international students pursuing bachelor's, master's, or doctoral degrees at participating universities in China. It is positioned as a major international funding opportunity for students.

stories.title: ANSO-CAS-TWAS/UNESCO PhD scholarships open for applications
stories.summary: Applications are open until February 28, 2027, for PhD scholarships at the University of Science and Technology of China and the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences. The program supports hundreds of postgraduate candidates annually, with a specific sub-category for TWAS/UNESCO selections.

stories.title: PM-YASASVI scholarship scheme details released
stories.summary: The Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment is implementing the PM-YASASVI scheme to provide financial assistance to students from Other Backward Classes, Economically Backward Classes, and nomadic tribes. Eligible students in classes 9 to 12 can receive support for tuition and hostel expenses.

stories.title: University of Ghana and Manchester announce dual PhD scholarships
stories.summary: The University of Ghana and the University of Manchester are inviting applications for nine dual PhD scholarships in development studies. The research program focuses on Africa's green energy transition and digital transformation. It is delivered through the Institute of Statistical, Social and Economic Research.

stories.title: Punjab Board releases 2027 exam datesheet
stories.summary: The Punjab School Education Board has released the practical and theory exam timetable for classes 8, 10, and 12. The announcement follows the standard schedule for state board examinations.

stories.title: UP Board practical exam dates 2027 announced
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh Madhyamik Shiksha Parishad has scheduled Class 10 and 12 practical exams for January 11 to January 28, 2027. Class 10 students will resume science and home science practical assessments, which carry 30 marks each, after a long gap. The board is returning to tradition.

stories.title: UGC NET December 2026 city intimation slips delayed
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency has not released the city intimation slips for the December 2026 UGC NET as of November 24. The agency previously indicated the information would be available 21 days before the exam. It now expects to release the details by November 25.

stories.title: SSC CHSL city intimation slips released
stories.summary: The Staff Selection Commission has released city intimation slips for the Tier 1 Combined Higher Secondary Level Examination. Candidates can view their assigned exam city on the official website ahead of the tests, which run from December 3 to December 31. The slip is not an admit card.

stories.title: UK student visa financial requirements to increase
stories.summary: The UK Home Office is raising the minimum bank balance requirements for international students starting November 30. Indian students planning to study in the UK from January 2027 must demonstrate higher funds to cover living expenses. The change follows the latest update to the Immigration Rules.

stories.title: UK student visa bank balance rules explained
stories.summary: Applicants for UK student visas must maintain required funds for 28 consecutive days to satisfy Home Office rules. Deposits made immediately before the November 30 threshold increase will not count toward the new proof of funds requirement. Timing remains a factor for those preparing bank statements.

stories.title: UK raises student visa financial requirements for Indian students - NewsBytes
UK student visa living cost thresholds rise
stories.summary: From November 30, the monthly living expense requirement for UK student visa applicants will increase to £1,570 for London and £1,203 for outside London. For a nine-month course, this brings the total required threshold to £14,130 for London and £10,827 for universities elsewhere.

stories.title: Afghan women denied UK student visas
stories.summary: Afghan women who secured scholarships to UK universities are unable to travel due to a government suspension of student visa processing for Afghan nationals. Affected students have urged the British government to reconsider the policy, which has halted their academic plans and left many without their opportunities.

stories.title: UK visa restrictions disrupt Afghan students
stories.summary: The UK government suspended student visas for nationals of Afghanistan, Sudan, Myanmar, and Cameroon in March 2026. The policy has prevented Afghan women who earned university places and scholarships from traveling to Britain. The restrictions remain in place for all nationals of the four countries.

stories.title: Afghan women face visa barriers to UK study
stories.summary: The UK Home Office implemented an emergency visa brake on study applications from Afghanistan, Sudan, Myanmar, and Cameroon in March. The policy has blocked Afghan women from pursuing university offers and scholarships. Applicants describe the loss of these educational opportunities as a significant personal setback.

stories.title: UK visa brake impacts Afghan university applicants
stories.summary: A Home Office visa brake introduced in March has blocked Afghan nationals from studying in the UK. The policy applies to scholarship candidates and those holding university offers. Universities have disputed the evidence base for the restrictions while the government continues to enforce the current visa threshold.

stories.title: Australia reviews student visa financial requirements
stories.summary: The Department of Home Affairs is seeking feedback on reforms to the Genuine Student requirement and financial capacity framework. Assistant Minister Julian Hill stated the review aims to ensure international students are appropriately prepared for academic and financial commitments while maintaining the integrity of the student visa program.

stories.title: IIT Kanpur opens new computer lab for EWS students
stories.summary: IIT Kanpur has inaugurated a modernized computer lab and the second phase of the Smt Sharda Singh Bhawan at its Opportunity School. The facility aims to provide children from economically weaker sections with improved access to digital learning and opportunities to develop essential computer skills.

stories.title: Google funds AI research at IIT Kharagpur
stories.summary: Google has announced $5 million in funding for IIT Kharagpur to support AI research in fields including agriculture, materials science, and Indic languages. The initiative aims to strengthen the institute's AI infrastructure and expand training opportunities for students, faculty, and teachers.

stories.title: Digital economy: BSMH 7.0 targets students with skills, entrepreneurship opportunities - The Nation Newspaper
Teachers report need for English learner training
stories.summary: A survey of 1,122 educators found that many mainstream classroom teachers lack training in providing language support for English learners. Respondents emphasized a need for more instruction on teaching language through academic content. Educators identified training as a primary strategy for serving these students.

stories.title: Georgia invests in Pyramid Model for early education
stories.summary: Georgia’s Department of Early Care and Learning is investing in the Pyramid Model to help teachers manage classrooms and social-emotional development. An initial evaluation by Child Trends found that foundational training and individualized classroom coaching were linked to teacher support. The state is now focusing on these methods.

stories.title: UNESCO calls for teacher training that fits working lives
stories.summary: UNESCO and the International Task Force on Teachers for Education 2030 argue that professional learning should be a right for every teacher. They suggest that working conditions must allow time for colleagues to discuss new approaches. The new Global Report on Teachers advocates for these career-long support structures.

stories.title: NTI and UBEC launch nationwide teacher training
stories.summary: The National Teachers’ Institute and the Universal Basic Education Commission have started a five-day training programme for 3,700 teachers and managers. Focused on Structured Pedagogy Strategies, the initiative aims to improve teaching and learning. The programme was inaugurated at the institute's headquarters in Kaduna this week.

stories.title: NCTE expands MITRA mentoring initiative
stories.summary: The National Council for Teacher Education is strengthening its national mentoring initiative, MITRA, to provide teachers with ongoing guidance. Under NEP 2020, the programme connects educators with professionals to share knowledge. The network is not limited to school teachers, as it also includes various external experts.

stories.title: Minister Abdul Mu'ti delivers National Teacher's Day speech
stories.summary: Minister of Primary and Secondary Education Abdul Mu'ti addressed National Teacher's Day on November 25, 2026. His speech covered teacher welfare, employment status, and competency development. The ministry released the official text earlier that week for use in commemorative ceremonies held across various regions of the country.

stories.title: Liberia education ministry targets teaching profession prestige
stories.summary: The Ministry of Education is launching reforms to improve the status of the teaching profession through better recognition and professional development. Education Minister Dr. Jarso Marley Jallah stated the government aims to make teaching an attractive career. The initiative follows recent Presidential Awards for Excellence in Teaching.

stories.title: Alberta backtracks on school flagpole regulations
stories.summary: The Alberta government will no longer require schools to install a second flagpole to fly both the provincial and Canadian flags. Education Minister Demetrios Nicolaides said the province is listening to partners after hearing cost concerns. Schools may now display both flags using a single pole.

stories.title: Manitoba expands school tech ban to wearables
stories.summary: Manitoba has updated its cellphone ban to include smart watches and AI glasses. Education Minister Tracy Schmidt issued a directive to school leaders last week, citing the need to ensure healthy learning environments. The original ban on mobile devices has been in place since September 2024.

stories.title: Chandigarh school hosts CBSE capacity-building session
stories.summary: St Joseph’s Senior Secondary School recently held a CBSE capacity-building programme focused on the National Curriculum Framework for School Education 2023. Sixty teachers participated in interactive activities exploring competency-based education and inclusive classrooms. The session also introduced the Prashast app for practical use in schools.

stories.title: Bihar CM orders university infrastructure completion by 2027
stories.summary: Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary has directed officials to finish construction projects at Pataliputra, Purnea, and Patna universities by March 2027. The review meeting covered schemes worth over 100 crore rupees. The government is also seeking better branding for agricultural products to expand their reach into international markets.

stories.title: Dallas ISD renames school for Shirley Ison-Newsome
stories.summary: The Dallas Independent School District has renamed the Harry Stone Montessori International Baccalaureate Academy to honor educator Shirley Ison-Newsome. A dedication ceremony is scheduled for November 19. The board approved the change earlier this year to recognize her long-standing leadership within the district and the local campus.

stories.title: Delhi nursery admissions criteria published
stories.summary: Private schools in Delhi have begun releasing admission criteria for the 2027-28 session, with home-school distance serving as a primary factor. Schools are awarding up to 70 points for proximity. The Directorate of Education's module for uploading these criteria was reported as non-operational on Monday evening.

stories.title: Ranchi schools begin Class XI admission process
stories.summary: City schools have announced cut-offs and entrance tests for Class XI students ahead of upcoming board exams. Provisional registration is open, with stream-specific requirements for English, mathematics, and science. Some institutions are offering tuition fee waivers based on student performance in pre-board and half-yearly examinations.

stories.title: Michael Taylor appointed head at Anchors Academy
stories.summary: Michael Taylor has joined Anchors Academy as Designated Head of School for Primary and Junior Secondary. He returns to Hong Kong after leading international schools in Tokyo and Kyoto. Taylor will oversee the development of the academy's K-12 through-train pathway and its newly launched junior secondary program.

stories.title: IIM Jammu and South Asian University sign partnership
stories.summary: IIM Jammu and South Asian University have signed a memorandum of understanding to collaborate on research and academic innovation. The agreement includes a provision to develop jointly conferred degree programmes. The partnership is described as a milestone in the internationalisation of management education for both institutions.

stories.title: IIM Jammu and South Asian University formalize collaboration
stories.summary: IIM Jammu and South Asian University have signed a memorandum of understanding to boost global academic outreach. The collaboration aims to create an ecosystem for research, entrepreneurship, and leadership development. The agreement was signed by the directors of both institutions in New Delhi on Tuesday.

stories.title: Nepal agrees to host offshore IIT campus
stories.summary: Nepal and India have agreed to establish an offshore campus of the Indian Institute of Technology in Nepal. The project follows a state visit by Prime Minister Balendra Shah to India. Stakeholders now note that creating a legal and regulatory framework is essential to move forward.

stories.title: Chandigarh school hosts annual sports day
stories.summary: Saint Soldier International School in Chandigarh held its annual sports day for students in classes VI to VIII. The event included track races, taekwondo, and yoga demonstrations. The school administration and local officials attended the celebration, which featured a variety of physical activities for the students.

stories.title: UGC chief pushes for industry-linked universities
stories.summary: University Grants Commission Chairman Prof Mamun Ahmed has urged universities to establish industry advisory boards and liaison offices to improve student employment. He also called for mandatory internships for all students within five years, promising financial support for institutions that link research and innovation with industry needs.

stories.title: India to open third offshore IIT in Nepal
stories.summary: India and Nepal have agreed to establish an offshore campus of the Indian Institute of Technology. This will be the third such international location for the institution, following existing campuses in Zanzibar and Abu Dhabi. The agreement was confirmed in a joint statement by both nations.

stories.title: Maharashtra CM meets task force on exam security
stories.summary: Maharashtra Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis met with Nandan Nilekani and former ISRO Chairman S Somanath to discuss examination reforms. The task force was formed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi to ensure a transparent and reliable testing system through the increased use of technology.

stories.title: Syracuse University adds AI to admissions
stories.summary: Syracuse University is using technology to conduct the initial review of undergraduate applicant transcripts. A senior official stated that the final stages of the admissions process will remain entirely human. The university did not specify which AI tools are performing the preliminary evaluations.

stories.title: Registration opens for CMAT 2027
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency has opened applications for the Common Management Admission Test 2027. The exam is scheduled for February 11 and will be conducted in a computer-based format. It serves as a national-level entrance test for management programs at participating institutions.

stories.title: CMAT 2027 application process begins
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency has opened the application window for the CMAT 2027 management entrance exam. Candidates can register through the official website until December 20. The examination is set to take place on February 11 for the 2027-28 academic session.

stories.title: KEA adjusts PG medical seat allotment
stories.summary: The Karnataka Examinations Authority has announced a revised procedure for its second round of PG medical seat allotment. Candidates have until November 25 to exit the process. The authority will re-run the allotment using existing preferences to account for seats vacated by students choosing other options.

stories.title: Insider Information: Visa Hurdles and Costs Drive Drop in International Enrollment - U.S. News & World Report
Palestinian students reach Ireland after visa delays
stories.summary: Twenty Palestinian students from Gaza are traveling to Ireland to begin their university studies. The group faced a four-month visa delay after the Irish Department of Justice initially rejected their applications. The students secured their travel after a public campaign highlighted the difficulties of obtaining documentation from Gaza.

stories.title: Gaza students secure visas for Irish universities
stories.summary: Twenty Palestinian students are traveling to Ireland to pursue university scholarships after a four-month visa dispute. The Irish government initially rejected the applications due to missing documentation, which students could not provide due to the destruction of local banking and postal systems in Gaza.

stories.title: Spain opens scholarship cycle for international students
stories.summary: The Spanish Ministry of Education has launched its 2026 to 2027 scholarship cycle for international graduates. The program offers support ranging from full tuition coverage to monthly living allowances and research funding. Application windows for the various grants are scheduled to open between December 2026 and January 2027.

stories.title: Applications open for Better Futures Fellowship
stories.summary: The Better Futures Fellowship is accepting applications for a nine-week program focused on research and fieldbuilding. The fellowship aims to improve the long-term future of humanity. Participants will engage in a facilitated discussion course followed by a project phase requiring the creation of a public output.

stories.title: SparkUp Initiative Fellowship 2027 announced
stories.summary: The SparkUp Initiative Fellowship is accepting applications for a capacity-building program aimed at women-led organizations. The initiative provides training in fundraising strategy and project development. It is open to organizations working across various sectors, including education, health, and environmental justice, with a deadline of December 20.

stories.title: Commonwealth Study Conferences 2027 applications open
stories.summary: Applications are open for the 2027 Commonwealth Study Conferences, a program for emerging leaders. Participants will travel in diverse study groups to visit industries and communities. The conference format includes no lectures or resolutions, continuing a tradition that began in 1956 for leaders across the Commonwealth.

stories.title: Robertson Foundation opens leadership lab applications
stories.summary: The Robertson Foundation is accepting applications for its 2027 Global Governance Leadership Lab. The 16-week virtual program pairs fellows with public service professionals to work on policy projects and leadership development. The experience is fully funded and concludes with a virtual capstone presentation.

stories.title: UNT reduces budget deficit by 89 percent
stories.summary: The University of North Texas reported a year-end deficit of less than $5 million, down from a projected $45 million. The university achieved this reduction through department consolidation and phasing out low-demand programs, despite a decline in international student enrollment caused by federal visa hurdles.

stories.title: Oregon State students visit state capitol for International Education Week
stories.summary: Thirteen Oregon State University students joined peers from five other universities at the state capitol on Nov. 18. The group met with legislative and regulatory staff to discuss international student issues and study abroad initiatives. The students reported that the visit felt more interactive than previous trips.

Victoria lacks public transport concessions for postgraduate students
stories.summary: Victoria is the only Australian state that does not provide public transport concessions to postgraduate students. The government aims to be a global leader in education, yet a new report suggests many students are walking because they cannot afford the tram. Goals are being set for the commute.

stories.title: Government suggests visitor visas for international students
stories.summary: The government has tightened student visa rules while suggesting that some students use visitor visas to finish their qualifications. The move aims to address integrity concerns but risks stripping students of protections. The government is now pointing students toward the very system it spent months trying to restrict.
